title: IAPO: Influence-Aware Policy Optimization for Credit Assignment in Multi-Turn Service Agents
abstract: arXiv:2608.24588v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large Language Model (LLM) agents increasingly solve long-horizon tasks through multi-turn interactions with users and external tools. In these settings, relevant task information often unfolds over time rather than being fully specified at the initial prompt. Service agents make this challenge especially concrete: users may clarify or revise their goals, while tool responses provide information needed for subsequent decisions. Thus, a final reward alone cannot indicate which actions contributed to resolving the task. Recent methods rely on comparative evidence from other trajectories or resampled continuations, or on separately constructed step-level learning signals, to refine credit. However, a completed rollout already records how information and errors flow between agent actions. We introduce Influence-Aware Policy Optimization (IAPO), which represents each rollout as a typed influence-dependency graph over trainable agent actions,

translated_title: IAPO：面向多轮服务智能体信用分配的影响感知策略优化
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.24588v1 公告类型：新 摘要：大型语言模型（LLM）智能体通过与用户和外部工具的多轮交互，日益解决长时程任务。在这些场景中，相关任务信息通常随时间逐步展开，而非在初始提示中完全指定。服务智能体使这一挑战尤为具体：用户可能澄清或修改目标，而工具响应则提供后续决策所需的信息。因此，单一最终奖励无法指示哪些行动有助于解决任务。近期方法依赖于其他轨迹或重采样续段的比较证据，或单独构建的步骤级学习信号，来细化信用分配。然而，一个完整的交互记录已经捕捉了信息流和错误如何在智能体行动间传播。我们引入了影响感知策略优化（IAPO），该方法将每次交互表示为一个在可训练智能体行动上的类型化影响依赖图。
tldr: IAPO通过构建类型化影响依赖图来显式建模多轮服务智能体中行动间的信息与错误传播，从而改进信用分配，无需依赖外部比较信号。
en_tdlr: IAPO improves credit assignment in multi-turn service agents by explicitly modeling information and error propagation between actions via a typed influence-dependency graph, without relying on external comparative signals.
